subject: math

objective.text: Tell time to five minutes. Use a.m. for morning and p.m. for afternoon and night.

source_ref.section: Lesson objective: Tell time to the nearest five minutes; relate a.m. and p.m. to time of day.

explanations.title: The clock shows the same time twice
explanations.text: A clock looks the same in the morning and at night. It cannot tell us which one it is.

source_ref.section: Concept Development

explanations.title: a.m. and p.m.
explanations.text: a.m. is from midnight to noon: the morning. p.m. is from noon to midnight. A comes before P, like morning before afternoon.

source_ref.section: Concept Development: 'an easy way to remember a.m. and p.m.'

explanations.title: Digital clocks
explanations.text: A digital clock shows the time with digits, like 7:35. It has no hands.

source_ref.section: Concept Development: 'Why do you think it's called a digital clock?'

examples.title: Waking up is a.m.
examples.text: You wake up for school in the morning. The sun is rising. So it is a.m.

assets_required.why_this_method: Hand positions must be exact, and the hour hand must move partway between numbers. Diffusion cannot do this.
assets_required.description: An analog clock with numbers 1-12, minute marks, an hour hand and a minute hand. Can also show a digital readout.
must_show_exactly: Numbers 1-12 in correct positions, 60 minute marks
Minute hand points exactly at the stimulus minute
Hour hand sits between hours in proportion to the minutes (for example halfway between 3 and 4 at 3:30)
Digital readout shows hh:mm with a.m. or p.m.
states_or_frames: any time hh:mm from the stimulus
assets_required.interaction: Display, or the child drags the hands. The tutor sets the time from the question stimulus.

visual_generation_rules: Diffusion cannot count reliably. Any picture where an exact number of objects matters must be built by code (SVG or widget) or drawn by an artist.

Every visual must be checked by a person: the count shown must equal the stimulus in the question and the rubric answer key.
Animations are described as frames with exact counts per frame, so they can be built or generated and then checked frame by frame.
Visual explanations are valid only when the asset exists (pipeline doc, Planner rules).
